item.title: AI ‘Chipflation’ Washes Ashore in the UK Economy
item.description: UK consumer prices will grab headlines in the coming week, with an AI-driven memory-chip shortage and higher energy costs keeping the Bank of England on guard.

item.title: Bond Traders Agonize Over AI Companies’ $70 Billion of Shadow Credit Backstops
item.description: Even before Nvidia Corp.’s splashy $500 billion financing partnership this week, investors were starting to fret over the roughly $70 billion in phantom liabilities that don’t appear on major AI companies’ balance sheets, but could materialize at the worst possible time.

item.title: Peru’s Economy Unexpectedly Slows as Fishing, Agriculture Slump
item.description: Peru’s economy unexpectedly slowed in June due to a slump in fishing and agriculture output amid unusual weather conditions.

item.title: ‘Outlier’ S&P 500 Earnings Strength Cheers Wall Street’s Bulls
item.description: Corporate America is blowing past Wall Street’s expectations for a stellar earnings season, adding to the rosy backdrop for a stock market trading near a record high.

item.title: As Global Waterways Face Squeeze, Mexico Pitches CIIT as Alternative Corridor
item.description: With waterways from the Panama Canal to the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea facing disruptions, Mexico is pitching a land route in the south as an alternative for global trade.

item.title: In the Inflation Ballpark
item.description: We’re not at target yet.

item.title: How India’s Future May Turn on Its Coming Census
item.description: The census will raise sensitive questions about economic benefits and their distribution.

item.title: Colombia’s $10 Billion Earthquake Bill Imperils Austerity Drive
item.description: Less than half an hour before the first market open of his presidency, Abelardo de la Espriella’s fiscal plan was shattered by the earthquake that devastated western Colombia.

item.title: Alibaba AI Models Hit 3 Billion Downloads, Passing Meta, Google
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding’s open-weight models have accumulated more than 3 billion global downloads in the past six months, eclipsing Meta Platforms Inc., Alphabet Inc. and domestic peers to become the world’s No. 1 artificial-intelligence model.

item.title: World Economy Latest: US CPI Softens, UK Economy Expands
item.description: Underlying US inflation showed few signs of accelerating in July as the energy-price shock from the war in Iran continued to fade, reinforcing the case for the Federal Reserve to hold off on interest-rate hikes in the near term.

item.title: China Film’s Sales Soar as Online Scorn Attracts Curious Viewers
item.description: A Chinese animated film that generated only about $1,000 in ticket sales in its first 10 days at theaters became a social-media sensation after online ridicule helped propel its box-office revenue into six figures, according to local media reports.

item.title: Xi Urges Shift to Prevention in Disaster Management, Xinhua Says
item.description: President Xi Jinping called for China to shift disaster management toward prevention, saying safety and resilience should be integrated into planning and development, Xinhua News Agency reported on Saturday.

item.title: Mastercard Says Brief Australia Payment Disruption Is Resolved
item.description: Mastercard card payments were temporarily declined for some Australian customers on Saturday afternoon because of a global issue that has since been resolved, according to the company.

item.title: Malaysia’s Anwar Vows Faster Reforms After Electoral Defeats
item.description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he will speed up the pace of reforms and strengthen an anti-corruption drive as he seeks to rebuild public support after a string of electoral defeats and party departures.

item.title: Money Managers Chase €500 Billion Historic German Pension Shift
item.description: One of the biggest reforms in Germany’s pension system since Chancellor Otto von Bismarck founded it in the late 19th century is about to hand modern fund managers a new empire of cash to deploy.

item.title: Germany’s Market-Friendly Pension Overhaul: Q&A
item.description: Germany is turning to capital markets to help fix its creaking retirement system.

item.title: China Protests Japan PM, Defense Minister’s Yasukuni Actions
item.description: China lodged a formal protest with Japan after Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent an offering to Yasukuni shrine and Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi visited it on the anniversary of Japan’s surrender in World War II.

item.title: South Korea’s Lee Proposes Talks With North in Pursuit of Peace
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for dialogue with North Korea and pledged to take steps to reduce military tensions and establish peaceful coexistence on the peninsula in a Liberation Day address.

item.title: Modi Vows Chip Plants, Nuclear Reactors in India Growth Push
item.description: India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country would build more semiconductor plants and expand its fleet of nuclear reactors, as he reiterated his government’s resolve to make India a developed nation in the next two decades.

item.title: US, Canada Still See Sticking Points Before Deadline for 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canada’s chief trade negotiator told a government advisory group that there’s still a significant amount of work to do to reach an agreement that would stave off a new wave of US tariffs next week.

item.title: Singapore Stocks’ Record Run Gets ‘Goldilocks’ Boost From Growth
item.description: Singapore’s stocks have outperformed the world over the past month as their traditional strengths of high dividend yields and resilient balance sheets get a lift from a “Goldilocks” economic backdrop.

item.title: Bally’s Warns of Going Concern Doubt as It Seeks Fresh Liquidity
item.description: Bally’s Corp. warned investors of “substantial doubt” that it will be able to continue as a going concern as it risks running afoul of its agreement with lenders.

item.title: Lula’s Lead Over Bolsonaro Narrows in Brazil Election Poll
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s lead over right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro narrowed ahead of Brazil’s October presidential election, according to a new poll published Friday.

item.title: Nvidia Has $21 Billion SpaceX Stake, $30 Billion in Intel Shares
item.description: Nvidia Corp. on Friday disclosed a nearly $21 billion stake in Elon Musk’s SpaceX and a $30 billion one in Intel Corp.

item.title: Anthropic Revenue Ahead of IPO Surges Over 14-Fold in Second Quarter
item.description: Anthropic PBC is telling prospective investors its second-quarter revenue jumped at least 14-fold versus the same period a year ago, according to documents seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Amazon’s New User Agreement Seeks to Curb Class-Action Suits
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. reintroduced a clause in its user agreement that seeks to prevent shoppers from filing class-action lawsuits against the online retailer, inserting a legal buffer between itself and plaintiffs attorneys that it removed five years ago.

item.title: Berkshire Pads Delta, Alphabet Stakes as Abel Taps Cash Pile
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. increased its holdings in Delta Air Lines Inc. and Google parent Alphabet Inc. as Greg Abel began tapping into the company’s massive cash hoard.

item.title: Hedge Funds Halved Short Bets on Yen Since Joint Intervention
item.description: Hedge funds further dialed back on their wagers against the yen, signaling a reduction in negative sentiment surrounding the currency after the US and Japan’s historic joint intervention.

item.title: Leveraged ETFs Snap Back as Casino Crowd Mints $50 Billion
item.description: Three weeks ago, Wall Street’s casino crowd took a beating. AI stocks buckled, semiconductor shares tumbled and leveraged trades unraveled.

item.title: Codelco Overhauls Management Team as New CEO Seeks Turnaround
item.description: Codelco is overhauling management and splitting oversight of its operations into northern and central-southern units as new Chief Executive Officer Jorge Gómez seeks to stabilize mines and finances at one of the world’s largest copper producers.
